page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. It features 64 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, providing 64 vCPUs. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and operates on a KVM hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance in multi-core and single-core CPU execution, with stress-ng and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 25%. Cryptographic and extended instruction capabilities are also in the top 25%, supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is strong, though large-block uncached read and write operations fall into the average range. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, ray tracing, and image processing benchmarks also demonstrate top-quartile performance.

This instance is suited for compute-heavy workloads such as multi-threaded decompression, image processing, and database operations, where it achieves top-quartile PassMark database and Redis SET operation throughput. It also supports small-scale LLM inference, processing 2865.39 tokens per second on a 135M model, though performance drops to average levels for medium 7B models. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, which represents a key architectural tradeoff for disk-intensive tasks. The 2.0 GB RAM per core ratio makes it highly resource-dense for compute-bound tasks, offering qualitative cost efficiency by avoiding over-provisioning of memory.

However, the lack of local storage requires network-attached storage, and its memory-per-core ratio is not intended for memory-bound applications.
